{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Hosting/Services Agreement (IBM)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings (document reference: § 3.1 Term) 

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against our playbook and identified **two critical deviations**, **five high-severity deviations**, and a further set of medium and low items. Four rules came back **compliant** (exclusivity, non-compete, MFN and — subject to the verification note below — non-solicitation), so the Agreement does not restrict our freedom to procure, build or trade elsewhere.

The two critical items are commercial gating issues. First, on **IP ownership (§ 5.4 / Type II Materials construct)**, deliverables we pay for default to IBM ownership, with only an intra-Enterprise licence back and no modification or sublicensing rights, while our own Type I Materials must be licensed to IBM for external distribution; the Agreement also never confirms we retain rights in our Content and Customer Data. Second, on **limitation of liability (§ 9.1)**, the mutual cap floor is only $100,000 measured on charges "paid", there are no uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement, and § 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM's liability entirely for loss of or damage to our records and data — our principal risk in a hosting arrangement.

The high-severity items are asymmetries: a **one-way assignment restriction (§ 14.10)**, an **IP-only IBM indemnity paired with an open-ended Customer indemnity (§§ 8.1, 8.2(a)(3))**, **uncapped early termination charges (§ 3.4(b))** set out in documents IBM may unilaterally amend under § 13.1, and a **revocable Base Components licence (§ 12.1)** that does not reach our Affiliates or Subcontractors.

Four items sit at or near our walk-away thresholds and are listed in Section 3. One finding (non-solicitation) failed verification and must be re-checked before we rely on it.

## 2. Findings

| Sev | Rule | Status | Section | Issue in brief | Our ask |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers (Type II Materials construct) | Type II is the default, so IBM owns works created during the Service period; our licence back is limited to use within our Enterprise with no modification or sublicensing. We must license our Type I Materials to IBM for external distribution and onward authorisation. No confirmation we retain rights in Content, Customer Components or data. | Make Customer ownership (Type I) the default; confine IBM-owned Type II to pre-existing/generic IP with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back; limit IBM's licence in our Materials to performing the Services; confirm we retain all rights in Content/Customer Components with no joint ownership. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Deviation | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | Structure is mutual on a 12-month fee basis (fallback shape met), but the floor is $100,000 on charges "paid" only; no carve-outs for confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement; § 9.1(c)(2) wholly excludes liability for loss of or damage to our records and data. | Raise the mutual floor to $1,000,000 on "paid or payable" charges; add a mutual Excluded Claims provision; confirm the data-loss exclusion does not cover IBM's own security or confidentiality breaches. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.10 Assignment | Restriction binds Customer only (consent required, no affiliate or asset-sale carve-out) while IBM may assign freely, including to our competitors. No change-of-control termination right appears elsewhere. | Make consent mutual; add Customer affiliate/successor and substantially-all-assets carve-outs; bar assignment to our competitors; confirm our change of control triggers no IBM right. |
| High | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM | IBM indemnifies only for third-party IP infringement and states that is its entire obligation — nothing for breach of law, IBM-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Our § 8.2 indemnity is broad, covering any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services". | Add IBM indemnity prongs for breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; delete § 8.2(a)(3). Notice/control procedure (§ 8.1(a)–(b)) and uncapped indemnity payments (§ 9.1(a)) already work. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | § 3.4(b) conditions our convenience right on "early termination charges" of unspecified, uncapped amount set in Attachment A and Service Option Attachments, which IBM may unilaterally amend under § 13.1. | Delete the charge. Fallback: cap at three months' recurring charges if an early-termination fee is unavoidable. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 12.1 License | Grant is expressly "revocable" and names only "Customer" — no Affiliates (p0015) or Subcontractors (p0031), despite Content Administrators/Services Recipients being expected to include them. Neither § 14.17 nor § 14.10 cures this. | Extend to Affiliates and Subcontractors acting on our behalf; delete "revocable" and "solely"; make the licence irrevocable during the term, terminable only for uncured material breach under § 3.3; confirm transfer to a successor on a permitted § 14.10 assignment. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No sole-source, requirements or minimum-volume covenant. § 14.16 is expressly mutual. "Exclusive" appears only at §§ 4.3, 5.2, 5.4/12.1 in unrelated contexts; § 14.11 is a scope-of-use limit. | No redline. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No non-compete or field-of-use covenant. § 14.11 bars only resale; § 12.1 limits use to the Services; §§ 13.2 and 14.19 address IBM delivery and acceptable use. | No redline. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | Unqualified investigation right: any frequency, no prior notice (p0137 requires only attempted notice before restricting access or removing Content), no limit on access to our systems, no auditor confidentiality, no cost allocation; p0138 obliges us to hand over all relevant information on request. | Add once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site where practicable with no direct system access, IBM's cost unless an underpayment exceeds 5%. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 14.3 Choice of Law | New York law is our preferred position, but there is no venue, jurisdiction or arbitration provision anywhere (§ 14.4 waives jury trial; § 14.14 sets a limitations period only). | Add exclusive New York County court venue to the existing sentence, leaving choice of law unchanged. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | No express minimum or take-or-pay (§ 4.1, § 3.5), but undefined "early termination charges" under § 3.4(b) combined with equal-duration auto-renewal under § 3.2 create open-ended exit exposure functioning as take-or-pay for Services never received. | Convert § 3.4(b) into a true-up of IBM's unavoidable direct costs; confirm no minimum purchase or volume commitment; preserve the one-month exit right. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 3.2 Renewal | Each Service Option Attachment auto-renews for a term equal to the prior term, so a multi-year initial term (set under § 3.1) renews for another multi-year period. Non-renewal notice is 90 days. No cap on renewal Charges (§ 4.1 leaves pricing to the attachments). | Set renewal term at 12 months; cut our non-renewal notice to 30 days (IBM retains 90); add a 60-day IBM renewal reminder; cap renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | One month's notice for Customer (consistent with our position) and no IBM convenience right, but conditioned on uncapped externally-specified charges, and no refund of prepaid charges (§ 3.5 only accelerates our payment obligations). | Delete the open-ended charges and add a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Fallback: cap at three months' charges. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | § 3.5 addresses only our payment obligations; no transition, return, export or deletion language, and neither § 14.18 nor § 11.6 imposes exit obligations on IBM — despite our Content residing in IBM's e-business Hosting Environment. | Insert transition assistance, data return and deletion certification into § 3.5, which already survives termination under § 14.2. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | Care-and-skill warranty, authority and law-compliance covenant only; no conformance warranty for Deliverables/Materials, no no-malicious-code warranty, no stated remedy. § 5.4(c) puts all Materials "AS IS" and § 5.2 makes § 5.1 exclusive. | Add a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty with a repair/re-perform/refund remedy; carve the § 5.1 warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burden | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No price-parity or MFN obligation; § 4.1 simply sets charges in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. § 14.16 confirms each party may contract with others. | No redline. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Needs review (verification failed)** | § 14.8 Personnel | Reviewed as compliant: § 14.8 covers only supervision of own personnel, IBM's assignment rights and subcontracting; no solicit/hire/recruit/induce language found, and § 14.16 is a freedom-of-action provision. **This finding did not pass verification and should be re-confirmed before we rely on it.** | No redline pending re-verification. If a restriction is introduced by SOW or order document, hold to the fallback: mutual, 12 months from end of the individual's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | No insurance clause anywhere, yet IBM hosts the environment, holds risk of loss for Base Components (§ 14.12) and processes personal information on our behalf (§§ 14.18, 5.3). | Insert new § 14.12A requiring CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request, binding IBM only. Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

## 3. Walk-away items

These sit at (or, where noted, adjacent to) our playbook walk-away positions and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **§ 11.3 Suspected Violations — unlimited, unannounced investigation with potential access to our systems.** This is expressly the playbook walk-away position; the guardrails (frequency, notice, business hours, independent auditor, no direct system access, cost allocation) are the minimum acceptable landing.
2. **§ 3.2 Renewal — auto-renewal for a term equal in duration to the prior term.** A multi-year initial term set under § 3.1 rolling into another multi-year period is a walk-away item, and the 90-day non-renewal notice sits at the outer walk-away limit.
3. **No insurance obligation on IBM.** Per the playbook, a vendor processing personal data with no insurance is a walk-away; a short IBM-only insurance paragraph is required.
4. **§ 12.1 — revocable licence not extending to Affiliates or Subcontractors.** Assessed as close to the walk-away; removal of "revocable" and irrevocability during the term are non-negotiable elements of any deal.

We also flag, for escalation rather than as a formal walk-away, the combination of the **$100,000 liability floor with no confidentiality/data-security carve-out and the total exclusion of liability for loss of our data under § 9.1(c)(2)** — in a hosting arrangement this leaves our principal risk unrecovered.

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** on the two critical items (IP ownership/Customer Data; § 9.1 cap, "paid or payable", mutual Excluded Claims and the § 9.1(c)(2) exclusion) as the lead asks, framed as gating.
2. **Bundle the high-severity asymmetries** — § 14.10 assignment, § 8.1/§ 8.2(a)(3) indemnities, § 3.4(b) early termination charges and § 12.1 licence scope — as a single mutuality package.
3. **Escalate the walk-away items** in Section 3 to the business sponsor before the next negotiation session, and confirm the commercial appetite on the § 3.2 renewal term and renewal price cap.
4. **Re-verify the non-solicitation finding (§ 14.8)**; do not treat it as compliant until verification passes.
5. **Confirm the downstream documents** — Attachment A, the Service Option Attachments and the Order Form — since § 3.1 sets the initial term, § 4.1 sets Charges and § 3.4(b) sets termination charges by reference to them, and § 13.1 permits IBM to amend them unilaterally. We should review those before signature and consider a change-control constraint on § 13.1.
6. **Carry the fallbacks** already identified where the counterparty resists: three months' charges cap on early termination; 60-day non-renewal notice; and E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M on insurance."}
